messages.text:
"Rework the visual presentation of “Emberwake — The Ashen Crown” into an original 16-bit pixel-art JRPG inspired by the atmosphere, environmental detail, and expressive characters of Final Fantasy VI. Preserve the existing working gameplay systems and save functionality.

First, focus on Hearthfall as a polished visual prototype:
- Use authentic pixel-art sprites and tile sets, with crisp pixels, consistent pixel density, and no smoothing. Target a 320×180 logical viewport with integer scaling where practical.
- Use compact, expressive characters approximately 16×24 pixels, with distinct silhouettes, readable costumes, four-direction walking animations, and idle poses. Replace the current geometric figures.
- Build a dense, thoughtfully composed village using approximately 16×16-pixel tiles: textured stone paths, timber houses, layered rooftops, flowers, signs, market stalls, trees, and small environmental details. Avoid oversized empty ground tiles.
- Use a cohesive palette of warm amber lights, earthy village colors, and cool blue-purple shadows. Keep scenery readable rather than covering it with a dark filter.
- Replace modern pill-shaped in-game controls with compact, pixel-bordered JRPG windows, readable bitmap-style text, and dialogue boxes with original character portraits.
- Frame exploration at a scale that shows several buildings and characters together. Use foreground and background layers to give the village depth.
- Establish the Hearthfall festival through NPC activity, decorations, and a brief character-driven scene.
Complete this village, one conversation with a consequential choice, and one representative turn-based battle before adding more locations or expanding progression systems. If you need sprite sheets or tile-set assets to achieve this style, identify those requirements explicitly.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

104:     id, tier, col, sp: opts.sp ?? 1,
105:     name: opts.name || skill.name || id,
106:     kind: opts.kind || (skill.passive ? 'passive' : 'skill'),
107:     desc: opts.desc || skill.desc || '',
108:     icon: opts.icon || skill.icon || '✦',
109:     req: opts.req || [],

## Summary

I reworked "Emberwake — The Ashen Crown" into a 16-bit pixel-art JRPG prototype centered on **Hearthfall**, preserving all existing gameplay systems (battle, skills, gear, quests, save/load via localStorage).

### What was built

**Pixel-art foundation (`js/engine/pixel.js`)**
- `TAU`, `PAL` cohesive palette (warm amber lights, earthy village tones, cool blue-purple shadows), `CHAR_PALS`
- Crisp pixel primitives (`pr`, `px`, `lineV/H`, `box`, filled circles/polygons/ellipses) drawn at integer coordinates
- Bitmap font (6×8 cell), wrap/measure text, 9-slice pixel windows, pixel buttons/choices/cursor arrow
- Offscreen tile/sprite canvases, all rendered with `imageSmoothingEnabled = false`; CSS `image-rendering: pixelated`

**Characters (`js/engine/art.js`)**
- 16×24 logical-pixel sprites with distinct silhouettes, four-direction facing, idle bob + two-step walk animations
- Role-based costumes (elder, seer, witch, guard, smith, inn, merchant, child) with readable hats/cloaks/accents
- Pixel portraits (32×40 busts) and pixel battle enemies

**World renderer (`js/engine/world-render.js`)**
- Dense village built from ~16×16 tiles: textured stone paths, timber walls, layered thatch roofs, doors, flowers, signs, market stalls, trees/great trees, rocks, fences, pond, garden, brazier/lantern/crystal/chest/altar/portal objects
- Background distant ridge + y-sorted foreground objects/characters for FFVI-style depth; warm light pass at dusk/night; vignette

**Hearthfall map (`js/data/zones.js`)**
- Redesigned as a compact festival village: elder hall, inn, forge, player cottage, market stalls, central square with hearth crystal + festival braziers + paper lanterns, notice board, garden, pond, south gate; 7 NPCs with gentle wander behavior

**Viewport & camera (`js/main.js`, `js/world.js`)**
- Fixed 320×180 logical viewport, integer scaling (1–4×), centered; snapped 16px-tile camera; tile-based tap input

**UI (`js/engine/ui-core.js`, `css/style.css`)**
- Pixel dialogue window with original character portraits, bitmap text, numbered choices (keyboard/D-pad navigable), interact labels
- Pixel party HUD (name, level, HP/MP bars, zone banner, clock); pixel D-pad/action touch controls
- Dialogue/HUD/interact drawn on the canvas; DOM pill controls hidden in-game

**Verification**
- Loaded title → continue → world with zero runtime errors
- Elder Maro conversation with a three-way consequential choice (crown / ready / why) renders and advances
- Turn-based battle vs. two Ashlings renders with pixel UI, portraits, HP bars, action menu, no errors
- All JS files pass `node --check`

### Assumptions made
- No external sprite/tile sheets were available, so **all pixel art is procedurally drawn at runtime** (as the brief invited: "identify those requirements explicitly" — requirement = a hand-drawn 16×16 tileset + 16×24 character sprite sheets would replace the procedural draws).
- A 320×180 logical viewport scaled by an integer factor (max 4×); on very small screens the canvas letterboxes at native 320×180.
- Save/load continues to use the existing `localStorage` system; the save in `cap16` starts at the prologue (Maro choice/battle path intact).

The village, one conversation with a consequential choice, and one representative turn-based battle are complete; more locations/progression can be added on top of these preserved systems.
